User asked for grooming and implementation in one go, so implementation continues in this session on the RUNE-22 worktree.","date":"2026-09-13T13:28:40.671Z","id":"c-2026-09-13t13-28-40-671z"},{"type":"agent_session","sessionId":"ecfbb583-ed3e-4f1d-9e2a-fae7277da606","startedAt":"2026-09-13T13:28:40.625Z","status":"active","user":"Claude Code","date":"2026-09-13T13:28:40.625Z","enginePid":21456,"progressCount":0}],"branch":"flux/RUNE-22-gilded-purple-rune-in-cell-6-is-dropped-in-5-of-6-rows-cell-","planGateRunning":true,"planGateAttempts":0,"planGateMode":"loop-confirm","baselineCommit":"9f5fd742fe208726269b3ea8887c20b9b8d88b3f","body":"> **TL;DR** — On six-icon rows the gilded purple rune in cell 6 is framed in only one row of six. The icon-row locator places every band 4–8 px below the cells (or 8 px too tall), which puts the silver cell's light frame right at the border-detection threshold and lets the lattice drift 16–22 px right of the gold frame. Pin the band's bottom on the cells' dark bevel line and snap its height to the cells' width, stop rewarding rows with exactly one gilded cell, and lock it with a new fixture.

## Problem / Motivation

On a 2560x1440 Combinations panel with six-icon rows (`E:\Git\RuneshapeCaptures\incoming\2026-09-13-purple-gilded-missed.png`, capture region 663x715), every row has a gilded rune in cell 2 and a gilded purple rune in cell 6. The marker overlay frames all seven cell-2 runes but only one of the six purple cell-6 runes (row 4). The dropped cells are classified `Ambiguous` and skipped with a Debug-only log, so at the default Information level nothing shows.

## Root cause (measured on the capture)

The gold frame of cell 6 sits at x=273–275 / 322–324 in **every** row; the game draws all six identically. The difference is in `RuneIconFingerprinter.LocateIconRow`:

- The cells' true extent is 45 px tall with a **dark bevel line** (HSV value < 0.25, ≥78% of the icon strip's columns) at y=45, 153, 261, 369, 477, 585. The located bands were [9,53], [105,157], [224,268], [320,374], [439,483], [537,589]: 4–8 px low, or 53–55 px tall.
- `ScorePlacement` is flat across those shifts (cell count dominates and every shifted band still segments six cells), so `RowDistancePenalty` pulls the band down towards the text line, and the 53 px candidate (text height 28 × `IconToTextHeightRatio` 1.9) beats the 45 px one on tie-breaks.
- **Consequence 1 (rows 0, 2):** with the band 6–8 px low, border columns cover only 37–39 of the 39 rows `BorderColumnCoverage` demands. The silver-framed cell 5 and cell 4's right border drop out; `SegmentIconCells` pairs 169→223 (56 px) and 223→324; `RegulariseToLattice` then takes pitch 58 and width 52 from the decorated left-hand cells and rebuilds cell 6 at x=289.
- **Consequence 2 (rows 1, 3, 5):** a 53 px band makes `CellWidthMinRatio` reject the real 45 px right borders, cells pair one border too far (55–56 px), pitch inflates to 60, cell 6 lands at x=295.
- **Consequence 3 (all rows):** the ring-separation term `bestRing − restRing` rewards a band in which exactly one cell reads gold, so a row with two gilded cells is scored *against* its correct placement (both ≈0.30 → separation ≈0) and *for* the misplaced one (0.22 vs 0.04).

On the correct band [433,477] every border column covers 41–45 of 45 rows, and in row 4 (where cell 5's columns happened to scrape 39/39) segmentation is already right.

## Implementation plan

1. **Score the bevel in `ScorePlacement`** (`src/OCR/RuneIconFingerprinter.cs`). After `SegmentIconCells`, measure the fraction of `IsDarkAt` pixels along `y = bottom` over the x-span from the first cell's left to the last cell's right (span-relative, so two-icon rows on `2 Raw.png` score the same as six-icon rows). Add `fraction × BevelLineWeight` (new constant, ~40 000: above the ring term's ceiling of 6 000 and a 9 px text-distance penalty of 3 600, below one cell's 100 000). Reuses `IsDarkAt` and `DarkLineMaxValue`, which `LocateIconRowByInkRuns` already uses for the same line.
2. **Replace the ring-separation term** with the largest gap between consecutive rings sorted descending (the natural two-cluster split). A row with one or two gilded cells scores its correct band equally; a row with none stays near zero. Keep the 20 000 weight.
3. **Snap the band to square cells in `LocateIconRow`.** After the best placement is chosen, take the median width of its non-gilded cells; if it is within `SquareSnapTolerance` (new constant, 8 px) of the band height, keep `bottom` and set `top = bottom − width + 1`. Cells are square in the game, so the width — measured from dark borders — is the better height. Do not snap when fewer than two plain cells exist (single gilded cell rows on `2 Raw.png`).
4. **Fixture.** Copy the capture to `tests/fixtures/runeicons/2560x1440/6 Raw.png` (same 663x715 region as fixtures 1–5). Add `RuneTwoGildedRowFixtureTests` (`tests/src/OCR/`) modelled on `RuneNarrowRowFixtureTests`: 7 rows, icon counts [6,6,6,6,6,6,4], gilded at index 1 in every row and index 5 in rows 0–5; assert zero ring overlap with the existing 0.20/0.08 margins, `ExtractRowKeys` yields 2 keys in rows 0–5 and 1 in row 6, every cell height within [38,60], and each row's two keys are ≥16 bits apart.
5. **Regression.** `1 Raw.png` and `2 Raw.png` tests (`RuneIconFingerprinterFixtureTests`, `RuneNarrowRowFixtureTests`, `RuneMarkerFixtureTests`, `RuneCropStabilityDiagnostics`) must stay green; identity hashes are plate-anchored (`FindPlateBounds`) so a vertical band shift of ≤8 px must not move them.

Open Questions (non-blocking) — using default: the Debug-only "ambiguous — dropped" log stays at Debug; `ExtractRowKeys` runs per OCR cycle and an Information line there would spam.

## Acceptance criteria

- [ ] On `6 Raw.png`, rows 0–5 each yield exactly two gilded keys (cells 2 and 6) and row 6 yields one; no plain cell is gilded or ambiguous.
- [ ] Gilded rings ≥ 0.20 and plain rings ≤ 0.08 on `6 Raw.png`, with zero overlap.
- [ ] Every located band on `6 Raw.png` ends on the dark bevel line (bottom ∈ {45,153,261,369,477,585,693}) and is 45 px tall in the six-icon rows.
- [ ] All existing rune fixture tests pass unchanged.

## Recommended Tests

Fixture-level (`dotnet test tests/Tests.csproj --filter FullyQualifiedName~Rune`): the new fixture test above plus the four existing fixture classes. The unit test `SegmentIconCells_SyntheticBorderedCells_FindsEachCellAndFlagsTheGoldOne` covers the synthetic path and should be unaffected since it feeds `SegmentIconCells` directly.

structuredContent.body:
> **TL;DR** — On six-icon rows the gilded purple rune in cell 6 is framed in only one row of six. The icon-row locator places every band 4–8 px below the cells (or 8 px too tall), which puts the silver cell's light frame right at the border-detection threshold and lets the lattice drift 16–22 px right of the gold frame. Pin the band's bottom on the cells' dark bevel line and snap its height to the cells' width, stop rewarding rows with exactly one gilded cell, and lock it with a new fixture.

## Problem / Motivation

On a 2560x1440 Combinations panel with six-icon rows (`E:\Git\RuneshapeCaptures\incoming\2026-09-13-purple-gilded-missed.png`, capture region 663x715), every row has a gilded rune in cell 2 and a gilded purple rune in cell 6. The marker overlay frames all seven cell-2 runes but only one of the six purple cell-6 runes (row 4). The dropped cells are classified `Ambiguous` and skipped with a Debug-only log, so at the default Information level nothing shows.

## Root cause (measured on the capture)

The gold frame of cell 6 sits at x=273–275 / 322–324 in **every** row; the game draws all six identically. The difference is in `RuneIconFingerprinter.LocateIconRow`:

- The cells' true extent is 45 px tall with a **dark bevel line** (HSV value < 0.25, ≥78% of the icon strip's columns) at y=45, 153, 261, 369, 477, 585. The located bands were [9,53], [105,157], [224,268], [320,374], [439,483], [537,589]: 4–8 px low, or 53–55 px tall.
- `ScorePlacement` is flat across those shifts (cell count dominates and every shifted band still segments six cells), so `RowDistancePenalty` pulls the band down towards the text line, and the 53 px candidate (text height 28 × `IconToTextHeightRatio` 1.9) beats the 45 px one on tie-breaks.
- **Consequence 1 (rows 0, 2):** with the band 6–8 px low, border columns cover only 37–39 of the 39 rows `BorderColumnCoverage` demands. The silver-framed cell 5 and cell 4's right border drop out; `SegmentIconCells` pairs 169→223 (56 px) and 223→324; `RegulariseToLattice` then takes pitch 58 and width 52 from the decorated left-hand cells and rebuilds cell 6 at x=289.
- **Consequence 2 (rows 1, 3, 5):** a 53 px band makes `CellWidthMinRatio` reject the real 45 px right borders, cells pair one border too far (55–56 px), pitch inflates to 60, cell 6 lands at x=295.
- **Consequence 3 (all rows):** the ring-separation term `bestRing − restRing` rewards a band in which exactly one cell reads gold, so a row with two gilded cells is scored *against* its correct placement (both ≈0.30 → separation ≈0) and *for* the misplaced one (0.22 vs 0.04).

On the correct band [433,477] every border column covers 41–45 of 45 rows, and in row 4 (where cell 5's columns happened to scrape 39/39) segmentation is already right.

## Implementation plan

1. **Score the bevel in `ScorePlacement`** (`src/OCR/RuneIconFingerprinter.cs`). After `SegmentIconCells`, measure the fraction of `IsDarkAt` pixels along `y = bottom` over the x-span from the first cell's left to the last cell's right (span-relative, so two-icon rows on `2 Raw.png` score the same as six-icon rows). Add `fraction × BevelLineWeight` (new constant, ~40 000: above the ring term's ceiling of 6 000 and a 9 px text-distance penalty of 3 600, below one cell's 100 000). Reuses `IsDarkAt` and `DarkLineMaxValue`, which `LocateIconRowByInkRuns` already uses for the same line.
2. **Replace the ring-separation term** with the largest gap between consecutive rings sorted descending (the natural two-cluster split). A row with one or two gilded cells scores its correct band equally; a row with none stays near zero. Keep the 20 000 weight.
3. **Snap the band to square cells in `LocateIconRow`.** After the best placement is chosen, take the median width of its non-gilded cells; if it is within `SquareSnapTolerance` (new constant, 8 px) of the band height, keep `bottom` and set `top = bottom − width + 1`. Cells are square in the game, so the width — measured from dark borders — is the better height. Do not snap when fewer than two plain cells exist (single gilded cell rows on `2 Raw.png`).
4. **Fixture.** Copy the capture to `tests/fixtures/runeicons/2560x1440/6 Raw.png` (same 663x715 region as fixtures 1–5). Add `RuneTwoGildedRowFixtureTests` (`tests/src/OCR/`) modelled on `RuneNarrowRowFixtureTests`: 7 rows, icon counts [6,6,6,6,6,6,4], gilded at index 1 in every row and index 5 in rows 0–5; assert zero ring overlap with the existing 0.20/0.08 margins, `ExtractRowKeys` yields 2 keys in rows 0–5 and 1 in row 6, every cell height within [38,60], and each row's two keys are ≥16 bits apart.
5. **Regression.** `1 Raw.png` and `2 Raw.png` tests (`RuneIconFingerprinterFixtureTests`, `RuneNarrowRowFixtureTests`, `RuneMarkerFixtureTests`, `RuneCropStabilityDiagnostics`) must stay green; identity hashes are plate-anchored (`FindPlateBounds`) so a vertical band shift of ≤8 px must not move them.

Open Questions (non-blocking) — using default: the Debug-only "ambiguous — dropped" log stays at Debug; `ExtractRowKeys` runs per OCR cycle and an Information line there would spam.

## Acceptance criteria

- [ ] On `6 Raw.png`, rows 0–5 each yield exactly two gilded keys (cells 2 and 6) and row 6 yields one; no plain cell is gilded or ambiguous.
- [ ] Gilded rings ≥ 0.20 and plain rings ≤ 0.08 on `6 Raw.png`, with zero overlap.
- [ ] Every located band on `6 Raw.png` ends on the dark bevel line (bottom ∈ {45,153,261,369,477,585,693}) and is 45 px tall in the six-icon rows.
- [ ] All existing rune fixture tests pass unchanged.

## Recommended Tests

Fixture-level (`dotnet test tests/Tests.csproj --filter FullyQualifiedName~Rune`): the new fixture test above plus the four existing fixture classes. The unit test `SegmentIconCells_SyntheticBorderedCells_FindsEachCellAndFlagsTheGoldOne` covers the synthetic path and should be unaffected since it feeds `SegmentIconCells` directly.

content.content:
{"id":"RUNE-19","title":"Derive cell height from cell width — cells are square, but height is measured per row","status":"Todo","priority":"High","effort":"M","assignee":"unassigned","tags":["ocr","runes","bug"],"createdBy":"Agent","updatedBy":"Agent","history":[{"type":"activity","user":"Agent","date":"2026-09-13T12:56:09.766Z","comment":"Created ticket.","id":"a-2026-09-13t12-56-09-766z"}],"body":"## Symptom

Two things the user has reported repeatedly turn out to be one bug:

1. Markers look squished / mis-sized, "especially the ones that have overflown".
2. Runes in some rows classify as *ambiguous* (gold ring 0.110–0.190) instead of cleanly plain or cleanly gilded, so they get no marker at all.

## Measurement

On `tests/fixtures/runeicons/2560x1440/5 Raw.png` (live capture from the user's panel), `LocateIconRow` returns these row heights:

```
41, 42, 43, 45, 49, 53
```

The cells in that panel are **~52 square**. Width is now measured correctly — the lattice work (RUNE-16 / PR #22) fixed the horizontal geometry. The vertical extent is still found independently per row by scanning for the icon band, and it under-measures by up to 11px on rows where the band blends into the row text or the row is clipped.

Rows 5 and 7 of that capture are the ambiguous ones. A short box crops the gilded frame's top and bottom arcs out of the sample, which is exactly the part of the ring that carries the gold.

## The fix

Rune cells are square. Once the lattice has a confident cell **width**, the height is that width — the row's vertical placement is then a centring problem (where does the square sit), not a measurement problem.

Sketch:
- `RegulariseToLattice` already produces a confident `cellWidth`. Use it as the height.
- Keep `LocateIconRow`'s result only as a *centre* hint: place the square so its centre matches the detected band's centre, clamped inside the row zone.
- `RowDistancePenalty` (currently an unproven guard — the RUNE-12 fixture passes with it at 0) may become redundant once the height stops varying; check whether it can go.

## Why this is its own pass

This moves every cell's box by a few pixels, and the box is what `GoldHueRingProportion` samples. It changes **classification**, not just drawing — rows that currently read correctly could flip. It must be measured against all five fixtures before and after, not bolted onto a UI change.

input.message:
**CHANGES NEEDED** — the diagnosis is strong and I verified its core measurement independently, but **step 3 duplicates an open ticket (RUNE-19)**, its tolerance constant **does not cover the failures it is meant to fix**, and the fixture contains **two dark-line decoys the new 40,000-point term cannot distinguish from a real bevel**.

## What I verified as correct

Every cited symbol exists in `src/OCR/RuneIconFingerprinter.cs` and means what the plan says: `LocateIconRow` (line 371), `ScorePlacement` (line 424) with `cells.Count * 100_000` + `(bestRing - restRing) * 20_000` - `spread * 200` - `squareness * 20`, `RowDistancePenalty = 400` (line 171), `CellWidthMinRatio = 0.85` (line 151), `BorderColumnCoverage = 0.85` (line 118), `IsDarkAt` (line 934, HSV value < `DarkLineMaxValue` 0.25), `RegulariseToLattice` (line 622). The weight arithmetic in step 1 checks out: 9 px x 400 = 3,600, ring term ceiling ~5,200 at the plan's quoted 0.30/0.04 rings, one cell = 100,000.

**I measured the bevel on `tests/fixtures/runeicons/2560x1440/6 Raw.png` myself** and step 1's span-relative design is not just correct, it is load-bearing:

| y | dark span (x) | coverage over span | coverage over 0.80*width |
|---|---|---|---|
| 45 | 7–321 | 0.844 | 0.502 |
| 153 | 7–321 | 0.832 | 0.494 |
| 261/369/477/585 | 7–321 | 0.857 | 0.509 |
| **693** (row 6, 4 icons) | **7–213** | **0.870** | **0.340** |

Row 6 is the proof: an absolute-width measure reads 0.34 there and would fail, while span-relative reads 0.87 and matches the six-icon rows. **Acceptance criterion 3's inclusion of y=693 is correct** — that value is not in the plan's root-cause list, so it was unverified; it now is.

Also confirmed: `DetectCells` (line 312) re-runs `SegmentIconCells` on the band `LocateIconRow` returns, so a step-3 snap of `top` is safely re-segmented afterwards.

## Major 1 — step 3 duplicates and conflicts with open ticket RUNE-19

`RUNE-19` ("Derive cell height from cell width — cells are square, but height is measured per row", **Todo, High, effort M**) is the same work, and specifies it *differently*:

- **RUNE-19**: height = width **unconditionally**; `LocateIconRow`'s band is kept only as a **centre** hint; also asks whether `RowDistancePenalty` can be deleted.
- **RUNE-22 step 3**: height = width **only within 8 px**; band's **bottom** is kept as the anchor.

These are not compatible. If RUNE-22 lands first, RUNE-19 must rip it out and re-do it on a different anchor. **Decide and state it in the plan**: either RUNE-22 step 3 is dropped and left to RUNE-19, or RUNE-22 supersedes RUNE-19 and RUNE-19 is closed as absorbed. My recommendation is to **drop step 3 from RUNE-22** — steps 1 and 2 alone fix the reported bug (the bevel term pins the bottom and the max-gap term removes the one-gilded-cell bias), and RUNE-19 is the pass that is already scoped to validate a height change against every fixture.

## Major 2 — `SquareSnapTolerance = 8` does not cover the measured failures

If step 3 is kept, 8 px is the wrong constant, by the plan's own numbers and RUNE-19's:

- RUNE-22 "Consequence 2" measures bands **53–55 px** tall against a true cell width of **45** — a delta of **8 to 10 px**. The 55 px case is outside the tolerance and the 53 px case sits exactly on the boundary, where behaviour depends on whether the comparison is `<` or `<=` — the plan does not say which.
- RUNE-19 measures `LocateIconRow` returning heights **41, 42, 43, 45, 49, 53** on `5 Raw.png` against **~52 px** square cells — deltas up to **11 px**. Step 3 as written would **not fire at all** on the rows RUNE-19 documents as broken.

A tolerance whose stated purpose is "the width is the better height" but which declines to act precisely when width and height disagree most is self-defeating. Either justify 8 px against data that supports it, or adopt RUNE-19's unconditional form.

## Major 3 — dark-line decoys the bevel term cannot distinguish

My scan of `6 Raw.png` found two horizontal dark lines that are **not cell bevels** but score as well as or better than the real ones, span-relative:

- **y=700** — span x=0–232, coverage **0.867**. This is **7 px below row 6's true bevel at y=693** (coverage 0.870).
- **y=713** — span x=0–343, coverage **0.843** (the capture's bottom edge).

Under step 1, a band ending at y=700 earns 40,000 x 0.867 = 34,680 versus 34,800 for the correct one — a **120-point** difference. The only real discriminator left is `RowDistancePenalty`, worth ~1,400 for that 7 px shift. **Total margin ~1,500 out of 40,000, under 4%**, and `spread`/`squareness` swings of that size are ordinary.

The plan cannot fall back on the cell-count term here: its own root-cause section states "`ScorePlacement` is flat across those shifts (cell count dominates and every shifted band still segments six cells)". A 7 px decoy sits squarely inside the range the plan says cell count cannot resolve.

**Address this explicitly** — e.g. require the dark line to be bounded by the segmented cells' own border columns rather than any dark run across the span, or require a plausible band *top* as well as bottom, or state the expected margin per fixture row and pin row 6's bottom to 693 in the new test so a regression here fails loudly. Acceptance criterion 3 already pins the bottoms, which is good; the plan should name the decoys as the reason it matters.

## Minor 1 — the "plate-anchored" regression argument has a hole

Step 5 asserts "identity hashes are plate-anchored (`FindPlateBounds`) so a vertical band shift of <=8 px must not move them". `ExtractRowKeys` falls back to `Inset(cell.GlyphBounds, GlyphInsetRatio)` when `FindPlateBounds` returns null — on that path the hash **does** follow the band. The claim holds only for cells whose plate reads. Soften it, or note that `RuneCropStabilityDiagnostics` is what actually enforces it.

## Minor 2 — fixtures 3, 4 and 5 are unprotected

Step 5's regression list is technically accurate: `RuneRowGeometryDiagnostics` is the only class touching `3/4/5 Raw.png` and it contains **zero `Assert` calls** (all three methods are `Dump*`), so it cannot fail. But RUNE-22 changes row placement for *every* capture, and RUNE-19 states the same class of change "must be measured against all five fixtures before and after". Cheap fix: have the implementer run `DumpRowGeometry` before and after and paste the diff into the ticket.

## Housekeeping

- **Step 4 is already done and needs no build change.** `6 Raw.png` is on disk at **663x715**, matching fixtures 1–5, and `tests/Tests.csproj:34` copies it via the glob `fixtures\runeicons\**\*.png` — no csproj edit required. Worth saying so, so the implementer does not go looking.
- **Artifact flag (W1) — not applicable.** This plan is detection-geometry, not UI/UX: no new component, layout or interaction. The visible symptom is overlay framing, but nothing here is designed visually. No artifact needed.
- **Reground check was vacuous.** `.docs/release-notes/INDEX.md` does not exist — `.docs/` contains only `project-overview.md`. I regrounded against the board instead, which is how RUNE-19 surfaced.
- `RUNE-16` shows **Todo** on the board but landed in commit `6adde2e` (PR #22) — stale status, unrelated to this ticket, flagging only because the plan depends on `RegulariseToLattice` from it (which is present and correct).

## What to change before re-review

1. Resolve the RUNE-19 overlap — drop step 3, or supersede RUNE-19 explicitly.
2. If step 3 stays, re-derive `SquareSnapTolerance` against the 10–11 px deltas on record, and state `<` vs `<=`.
3. Add a guard or a stated margin for the y=700 / y=713 decoys.
4. Fix the plate-anchoring claim and add the before/after `DumpRowGeometry` run for fixtures 3–5.

The icon-row locator places every band 4–8 px below the cells (or 8 px too tall), which puts the silver cell's light frame right at the border-detection threshold and lets the lattice drift 16–22 px right of the gold frame. ## Problem / Motivation

On a 2560x1440 Combinations panel with six-icon rows (`E:\Git\RuneshapeCaptures\incoming\2026-09-13-purple-gilded-missed.png`, capture region 663x715), every row has a gilded rune in cell 2 and a gilded purple rune in cell 6. The marker overlay frames all seven cell-2 runes but only one of the six purple cell-6 runes (row 4). The dropped cells are classified `Ambiguous` and skipped with a Debug-only log, so at the default Information level nothing shows.

## Root cause (measured on the capture)

The gold frame of cell 6 sits at x=273–275 / 322–324 in **every** row; the game draws all six identically. The difference is in `RuneIconFingerprinter.LocateIconRow`:

- The cells' true extent is 45 px tall with a **dark bevel line** (HSV value < 0.25, ≥78% of the icon strip's columns) at y=45, 153, 261, 369, 477, 585. The located bands were [9,53], [105,157], [224,268], [320,374], [439,483], [537,589]: 4–8 px low, or 53–55 px tall.
- `ScorePlacement` is flat across those shifts (cell count dominates and every shifted band still segments six cells), so `RowDistancePenalty` pulls the band down towards the text line, and the 53 px candidate (text height 28 × `IconToTextHeightRatio` 1.9) beats the 45 px one on tie-breaks.
- **Consequence 1 (rows 0, 2):** with the band 6–8 px low, border columns cover only 37–39 of the 39 rows `BorderColumnCoverage` demands. The silver-framed cell 5 and cell 4's right border drop out; `SegmentIconCells` pairs 169→223 (56 px) and 223→324; `RegulariseToLattice` then takes pitch 58 and width 52 from the decorated left-hand cells and rebuilds cell 6 at x=289.
- **Consequence 2 (rows 1, 3, 5):** a 53 px band makes `CellWidthMinRatio` reject the real 45 px right borders, cells pair one border too far (55–56 px), pitch inflates to 60, cell 6 lands at x=295.
- **Consequence 3 (all rows):** the ring-separation term `bestRing − restRing` rewards a band in which exactly one cell reads gold, so a row with two gilded cells is scored *against* its correct placement (both ≈0.30 → separation ≈0) and *for* the misplaced one (0.22 vs 0.04).

On the correct band [433,477] every border column covers 41–45 of 45 rows, and in row 4 (where cell 5's columns happened to scrape 39/39) segmentation is already right.

## Implementation plan

1. **Score the bevel in `ScorePlacement`** (`src/OCR/RuneIconFingerprinter.cs`). After `SegmentIconCells`, measure the fraction of `IsDarkAt` pixels along `y = bottom` over the x-span from the first cell's left to the last cell's right (span-relative, so two-icon rows on `2 Raw.png` score the same as six-icon rows). Add `fraction × BevelLineWeight` (new constant, ~40 000: above the ring term's ceiling of 6 000 and a 9 px text-distance penalty of 3 600, below one cell's 100 000). Reuses `IsDarkAt` and `DarkLineMaxValue`, which `LocateIconRowByInkRuns` already uses for the same line.
2. **Replace the ring-separation term** with the largest gap between consecutive rings sorted descending (the natural two-cluster split). A row with one or two gilded cells scores its correct band equally; a row with none stays near zero. Keep the 20 000 weight.
3. **Snap the band to square cells in `LocateIconRow`.** After the best placement is chosen, take the median width of its non-gilded cells; if it is within `SquareSnapTolerance` (new constant, 8 px) of the band height, keep `bottom` and set `top = bottom − width + 1`. Cells are square in the game, so the width — measured from dark borders — is the better height. Do not snap when fewer than two plain cells exist (single gilded cell rows on `2 Raw.png`).
4. **Fixture.** Copy the capture to `tests/fixtures/runeicons/2560x1440/6 Raw.png` (same 663x715 region as fixtures 1–5). Add `RuneTwoGildedRowFixtureTests` (`tests/src/OCR/`) modelled on `RuneNarrowRowFixtureTests`: 7 rows, icon counts [6,6,6,6,6,6,4], gilded at index 1 in every row and index 5 in rows 0–5; assert zero ring overlap with the existing 0.20/0.08 margins, `ExtractRowKeys` yields 2 keys in rows 0–5 and 1 in row 6, every cell height within [38,60], and each row's two keys are ≥16 bits apart.
5. **Regression.** `1 Raw.png` and `2 Raw.png` tests (`RuneIconFingerprinterFixtureTests`, `RuneNarrowRowFixtureTests`, `RuneMarkerFixtureTests`, `RuneCropStabilityDiagnostics`) must stay green; identity hashes are plate-anchored (`FindPlateBounds`) so a vertical band shift of ≤8 px must not move them.

Open Questions (non-blocking) — using default: the Debug-only "ambiguous — dropped" log stays at Debug; `ExtractRowKeys` runs per OCR cycle and an Information line there would spam.

## Acceptance criteria

- [ ] On `6 Raw.png`, rows 0–5 each yield exactly two gilded keys (cells 2 and 6) and row 6 yields one; no plain cell is gilded or ambiguous.
- [ ] Gilded rings ≥ 0.20 and plain rings ≤ 0.08 on `6 Raw.png`, with zero overlap.

`RUNE-19` ("Derive cell height from cell width — cells are square, but height is measured per row", **Todo, High, effort M**) is the same work, and specifies it *differently*:

- **RUNE-19**: height = width **unconditionally**; `LocateIconRow`'s band is kept only as a **centre** hint; also asks whether `RowDistancePenalty` can be deleted.
- **RUNE-22 step 3**: height = width **only within 8 px**; band's **bottom** is kept as the anchor.

These are not compatible. If RUNE-22 lands first, RUNE-19 must rip it out and re-do it on a different anchor. **Decide and state it in the plan**: either RUNE-22 step 3 is dropped and left to RUNE-19, or RUNE-22 supersedes RUNE-19 and RUNE-19 is closed as absorbed. My recommendation is to **drop step 3 from RUNE-22** — steps 1 and 2 alone fix the reported bug (the bevel term pins the bottom and the max-gap term removes the one-gilded-cell bias), and RUNE-19 is the pass that is already scoped to validate a height change against every fixture.

## Major 2 — `SquareSnapTolerance = 8` does not cover the measured failures

If step 3 is kept, 8 px is the wrong constant, by the plan's own numbers and RUNE-19's:

- RUNE-22 "Consequence 2" measures bands **53–55 px** tall against a true cell width of **45** — a delta of **8 to 10 px**. The 55 px case is outside the tolerance and the 53 px case sits exactly on the boundary, where behaviour depends on whether the comparison is `<` or `<=` — the plan does not say which.
- RUNE-19 measures `LocateIconRow` returning heights **41, 42, 43, 45, 49, 53** on `5 Raw.png` against **~52 px** square cells — deltas up to **11 px**. Step 3 as written would **not fire at all** on the rows RUNE-19 documents as broken.

A tolerance whose stated purpose is "the width is the better height" but which declines to act precisely when width and height disagree most is self-defeating. Either justify 8 px against data that supports it, or adopt RUNE-19's unconditional form.

## Major 3 — dark-line decoys the bevel term cannot distinguish

My scan of `6 Raw.png` found two horizontal dark lines that are **not cell bevels** but score as well as or better than the real ones, span-relative:

- **y=700** — span x=0–232, coverage **0.867**. This is **7 px below row 6's true bevel at y=693** (coverage 0.870).
- **y=713** — span x=0–343, coverage **0.843** (the capture's bottom edge).

Under step 1, a band ending at y=700 earns 40,000 x 0.867 = 34,680 versus 34,800 for the correct one — a **120-point** difference. The only real discriminator left is `RowDistancePenalty`, worth ~1,400 for that 7 px shift. **Total margin ~1,500 out of 40,000, under 4%**, and `spread`/`squareness` swings of that size are ordinary.

The plan cannot fall back on the cell-count term here: its own root-cause section states "`ScorePlacement` is flat across those shifts (cell count dominates and every shifted band still segments six cells)". A 7 px decoy sits squarely inside the range the plan says cell count cannot resolve.

**Address this explicitly** — e.g. require the dark line to be bounded by the segmented cells' own border columns rather than any dark run across the span, or require a plausible band *top* as well as bottom, or state the expected margin per fixture row and pin row 6's bottom to 693 in the new test so a regression here fails loudly. Acceptance criterion 3 already pins the bottoms, which is good; the plan should name the decoys as the reason it matters.

## Minor 1 — the "plate-anchored" regression argument has a hole

Step 5 asserts "identity hashes are plate-anchored (`FindPlateBounds`) so a vertical band shift of <=8 px must not move them". `ExtractRowKeys` falls back to `Inset(cell.GlyphBounds, GlyphInsetRatio)` when `FindPlateBounds` returns null — on that path the hash **does** follow the band. The claim holds only for cells whose plate reads. Soften it, or note that `RuneCropStabilityDiagnostics` is what actually enforces it.

## Minor 2 — fixtures 3, 4 and 5 are unprotected

Step 5's regression list is technically accurate: `RuneRowGeometryDiagnostics` is the only class touching `3/4/5 Raw.png` and it contains **zero `Assert` calls** (all three methods are `Dump*`), so it cannot fail. But RUNE-22 changes row placement for *every* capture, and RUNE-19 states the same class of change "must be measured against all five fixtures before and after". Cheap fix: have the implementer run `DumpRowGeometry` before and after and paste the diff into the ticket.

- **Step 4 is already done and needs no build change.** `6 Raw.png` is on disk at **663x715**, matching fixtures 1–5, and `tests/Tests.csproj:34` copies it via the glob `fixtures\runeicons\**\*.png` — no csproj edit required. Worth saying so, so the implementer does not go looking.

The icon-row locator places every band 4–8 px below the cells (or 8 px too tall), which puts the silver cell's light frame right at the border-detection threshold and lets the lattice drift 16–22 px right of the gold frame. Pin the band's bottom on the cells' dark bevel line and snap its height to the cells' width, stop rewarding rows with exactly one gilded cell, and lock it with a new fixture.

## Problem / Motivation

On a 2560x1440 Combinations panel with six-icon rows (`E:\Git\RuneshapeCaptures\incoming\2026-09-13-purple-gilded-missed.png`, capture region 663x715), every row has a gilded rune in cell 2 and a gilded purple rune in cell 6. The marker overlay frames all seven cell-2 runes but only one of the six purple cell-6 runes (row 4). The dropped cells are classified `Ambiguous` and skipped with a Debug-only log, so at the default Information level nothing shows.

## Root cause (measured on the capture)

The gold frame of cell 6 sits at x=273–275 / 322–324 in **every** row; the game draws all six identically. The difference is in `RuneIconFingerprinter.LocateIconRow`:

- The cells' true extent is 45 px tall with a **dark bevel line** (HSV value < 0.25, ≥78% of the icon strip's columns) at y=45, 153, 261, 369, 477, 585. The located bands were [9,53], [105,157], [224,268], [320,374], [439,483], [537,589]: 4–8 px low, or 53–55 px tall.
- `ScorePlacement` is flat across those shifts (cell count dominates and every shifted band still segments six cells), so `RowDistancePenalty` pulls the band down towards the text line, and the 53 px candidate (text height 28 × `IconToTextHeightRatio` 1.9) beats the 45 px one on tie-breaks.
- **Consequence 1 (rows 0, 2):** with the band 6–8 px low, border columns cover only 37–39 of the 39 rows `BorderColumnCoverage` demands. The silver-framed cell 5 and cell 4's right border drop out; `SegmentIconCells` pairs 169→223 (56 px) and 223→324; `RegulariseToLattice` then takes pitch 58 and width 52 from the decorated left-hand cells and rebuilds cell 6 at x=289.
- **Consequence 2 (rows 1, 3, 5):** a 53 px band makes `CellWidthMinRatio` reject the real 45 px right borders, cells pair one border too far (55–56 px), pitch inflates to 60, cell 6 lands at x=295.
- **Consequence 3 (all rows):** the ring-separation term `bestRing − restRing` rewards a band in which exactly one cell reads gold, so a row with two gilded cells is scored *against* its correct placement (both ≈0.30 → separation ≈0) and *for* the misplaced one (0.22 vs 0.04).

On the correct band [433,477] every border column covers 41–45 of 45 rows, and in row 4 (where cell 5's columns happened to scrape 39/39) segmentation is already right.

## Implementation plan

1. **Score the bevel in `ScorePlacement`** (`src/OCR/RuneIconFingerprinter.cs`). After `SegmentIconCells`, measure the fraction of `IsDarkAt` pixels along `y = bottom` over the x-span from the first cell's left to the last cell's right (span-relative, so two-icon rows on `2 Raw.png` score the same as six-icon rows). Add `fraction × BevelLineWeight` (new constant, ~40 000: above the ring term's ceiling of 6 000 and a 9 px text-distance penalty of 3 600, below one cell's 100 000). Reuses `IsDarkAt` and `DarkLineMaxValue`, which `LocateIconRowByInkRuns` already uses for the same line.
2. **Replace the ring-separation term** with the largest gap between consecutive rings sorted descending (the natural two-cluster split). A row with one or two gilded cells scores its correct band equally; a row with none stays near zero. Keep the 20 000 weight.
3. **Snap the band to square cells in `LocateIconRow`.** After the best placement is chosen, take the median width of its non-gilded cells; if it is within `SquareSnapTolerance` (new constant, 8 px) of the band height, keep `bottom` and set `top = bottom − width + 1`. Cells are square in the game, so the width — measured from dark borders — is the better height. Do not snap when fewer than two plain cells exist (single gilded cell rows on `2 Raw.png`).
4. **Fixture.** Copy the capture to `tests/fixtures/runeicons/2560x1440/6 Raw.png` (same 663x715 region as fixtures 1–5). Add `RuneTwoGildedRowFixtureTests` (`tests/src/OCR/`) modelled on `RuneNarrowRowFixtureTests`: 7 rows, icon counts [6,6,6,6,6,6,4], gilded at index 1 in every row and index 5 in rows 0–5; assert zero ring overlap with the existing 0.20/0.08 margins, `ExtractRowKeys` yields 2 keys in rows 0–5 and 1 in row 6, every cell height within [38,60], and each row's two keys are ≥16 bits apart.
5. **Regression.** `1 Raw.png` and `2 Raw.png` tests (`RuneIconFingerprinterFixtureTests`, `RuneNarrowRowFixtureTests`, `RuneMarkerFixtureTests`, `RuneCropStabilityDiagnostics`) must stay green; identity hashes are plate-anchored (`FindPlateBounds`) so a vertical band shift of ≤8 px must not move them.

Open Questions (non-blocking) — using default: the Debug-only "ambiguous — dropped" log stays at Debug; `ExtractRowKeys` runs per OCR cycle and an Information line there would spam.

## Acceptance criteria

- [ ] On `6 Raw.png`, rows 0–5 each yield exactly two gilded keys (cells 2 and 6) and row 6 yields one; no plain cell is gilded or ambiguous.
- [ ] Gilded rings ≥ 0.20 and plain rings ≤ 0.08 on `6 Raw.png`, with zero overlap.
- [ ] Every located band on `6 Raw.png` ends on the dark bevel line (bottom ∈ {45,153,261,369,477,585,693}) and is 45 px tall in the six-icon rows.
- [ ] All existing rune fixture tests pass unchanged.

## Recommended Tests

Fixture-level (`dotnet test tests/Tests.csproj --filter FullyQualifiedName~Rune`): the new fixture test above plus the four existing fixture classes. The unit test `SegmentIconCells_SyntheticBorderedCells_FindsEachCellAndFlagsTheGoldOne` covers the synthetic path and should be unaffected since it feeds `SegmentIconCells` directly.

**CHANGES NEEDED** — the diagnosis is strong and I verified its core measurement independently, but **step 3 duplicates an open ticket (RUNE-19)**, its tolerance constant **does not cover the failures it is meant to fix**, and the fixture contains **two dark-line decoys the new 40,000-point term cannot distinguish from a real bevel**.

## What I verified as correct

Every cited symbol exists in `src/OCR/RuneIconFingerprinter.cs` and means what the plan says: `LocateIconRow` (line 371), `ScorePlacement` (line 424) with `cells.Count * 100_000` + `(bestRing - restRing) * 20_000` - `spread * 200` - `squareness * 20`, `RowDistancePenalty = 400` (line 171), `CellWidthMinRatio = 0.85` (line 151), `BorderColumnCoverage = 0.85` (line 118), `IsDarkAt` (line 934, HSV value < `DarkLineMaxValue` 0.25), `RegulariseToLattice` (line 622). The weight arithmetic in step 1 checks out: 9 px x 400 = 3,600, ring term ceiling ~5,200 at the plan's quoted 0.30/0.04 rings, one cell = 100,000.

**I measured the bevel on `tests/fixtures/runeicons/2560x1440/6 Raw.png` myself** and step 1's span-relative design is not just correct, it is load-bearing:

| y | dark span (x) | coverage over span | coverage over 0.80*width |
|---|---|---|---|
| 45 | 7–321 | 0.844 | 0.502 |
| 153 | 7–321 | 0.832 | 0.494 |
| 261/369/477/585 | 7–321 | 0.857 | 0.509 |
| **693** (row 6, 4 icons) | **7–213** | **0.870** | **0.340** |

Row 6 is the proof: an absolute-width measure reads 0.34 there and would fail, while span-relative reads 0.87 and matches the six-icon rows. **Acceptance criterion 3's inclusion of y=693 is correct** — that value is not in the plan's root-cause list, so it was unverified; it now is.

Also confirmed: `DetectCells` (line 312) re-runs `SegmentIconCells` on the band `LocateIconRow` returns, so a step-3 snap of `top` is safely re-segmented afterwards.

## Major 1 — step 3 duplicates and conflicts with open ticket RUNE-19

`RUNE-19` ("Derive cell height from cell width — cells are square, but height is measured per row", **Todo, High, effort M**) is the same work, and specifies it *differently*:

- **RUNE-19**: height = width **unconditionally**; `LocateIconRow`'s band is kept only as a **centre** hint; also asks whether `RowDistancePenalty` can be deleted.
- **RUNE-22 step 3**: height = width **only within 8 px**; band's **bottom** is kept as the anchor.

These are not compatible. If RUNE-22 lands first, RUNE-19 must rip it out and re-do it on a different anchor. **Decide and state it in the plan**: either RUNE-22 step 3 is dropped and left to RUNE-19, or RUNE-22 supersedes RUNE-19 and RUNE-19 is closed as absorbed. My recommendation is to **drop step 3 from RUNE-22** — steps 1 and 2 alone fix the reported bug (the bevel term pins the bottom and the max-gap term removes the one-gilded-cell bias), and RUNE-19 is the pass that is already scoped to validate a height change against every fixture.

## Major 2 — `SquareSnapTolerance = 8` does not cover the measured failures

If step 3 is kept, 8 px is the wrong constant, by the plan's own numbers and RUNE-19's:

- RUNE-22 "Consequence 2" measures bands **53–55 px** tall against a true cell width of **45** — a delta of **8 to 10 px**. The 55 px case is outside the tolerance and the 53 px case sits exactly on the boundary, where behaviour depends on whether the comparison is `<` or `<=` — the plan does not say which.
- RUNE-19 measures `LocateIconRow` returning heights **41, 42, 43, 45, 49, 53** on `5 Raw.png` against **~52 px** square cells — deltas up to **11 px**. Step 3 as written would **not fire at all** on the rows RUNE-19 documents as broken.

A tolerance whose stated purpose is "the width is the better height" but which declines to act precisely when width and height disagree most is self-defeating. Either justify 8 px against data that supports it, or adopt RUNE-19's unconditional form.

## Major 3 — dark-line decoys the bevel term cannot distinguish

My scan of `6 Raw.png` found two horizontal dark lines that are **not cell bevels** but score as well as or better than the real ones, span-relative:

- **y=700** — span x=0–232, coverage **0.867**. This is **7 px below row 6's true bevel at y=693** (coverage 0.870).
- **y=713** — span x=0–343, coverage **0.843** (the capture's bottom edge).

Under step 1, a band ending at y=700 earns 40,000 x 0.867 = 34,680 versus 34,800 for the correct one — a **120-point** difference. The only real discriminator left is `RowDistancePenalty`, worth ~1,400 for that 7 px shift. **Total margin ~1,500 out of 40,000, under 4%**, and `spread`/`squareness` swings of that size are ordinary.

The plan cannot fall back on the cell-count term here: its own root-cause section states "`ScorePlacement` is flat across those shifts (cell count dominates and every shifted band still segments six cells)". A 7 px decoy sits squarely inside the range the plan says cell count cannot resolve.

**Address this explicitly** — e.g. require the dark line to be bounded by the segmented cells' own border columns rather than any dark run across the span, or require a plausible band *top* as well as bottom, or state the expected margin per fixture row and pin row 6's bottom to 693 in the new test so a regression here fails loudly. Acceptance criterion 3 already pins the bottoms, which is good; the plan should name the decoys as the reason it matters.

## Minor 1 — the "plate-anchored" regression argument has a hole

Step 5 asserts "identity hashes are plate-anchored (`FindPlateBounds`) so a vertical band shift of <=8 px must not move them". `ExtractRowKeys` falls back to `Inset(cell.GlyphBounds, GlyphInsetRatio)` when `FindPlateBounds` returns null — on that path the hash **does** follow the band. The claim holds only for cells whose plate reads. Soften it, or note that `RuneCropStabilityDiagnostics` is what actually enforces it.

## Minor 2 — fixtures 3, 4 and 5 are unprotected

Step 5's regression list is technically accurate: `RuneRowGeometryDiagnostics` is the only class touching `3/4/5 Raw.png` and it contains **zero `Assert` calls** (all three methods are `Dump*`), so it cannot fail. But RUNE-22 changes row placement for *every* capture, and RUNE-19 states the same class of change "must be measured against all five fixtures before and after". Cheap fix: have the implementer run `DumpRowGeometry` before and after and paste the diff into the ticket.

## Housekeeping

- **Step 4 is already done and needs no build change.** `6 Raw.png` is on disk at **663x715**, matching fixtures 1–5, and `tests/Tests.csproj:34` copies it via the glob `fixtures\runeicons\**\*.png` — no csproj edit required. Worth saying so, so the implementer does not go looking.
- **Artifact flag (W1) — not applicable.** This plan is detection-geometry, not UI/UX: no new component, layout or interaction. The visible symptom is overlay framing, but nothing here is designed visually. No artifact needed.
- **Reground check was vacuous.** `.docs/release-notes/INDEX.md` does not exist — `.docs/` contains only `project-overview.md`. I regrounded against the board instead, which is how RUNE-19 surfaced.
- `RUNE-16` shows **Todo** on the board but landed in commit `6adde2e` (PR #22) — stale status, unrelated to this ticket, flagging only because the plan depends on `RegulariseToLattice` from it (which is present and correct).

## What to change before re-review

1. Resolve the RUNE-19 overlap — drop step 3, or supersede RUNE-19 explicitly.
2. If step 3 stays, re-derive `SquareSnapTolerance` against the 10–11 px deltas on record, and state `<` vs `<=`.
3. Add a guard or a stated margin for the y=700 / y=713 decoys.
4. Fix the plate-anchoring claim and add the before/after `DumpRowGeometry` run for fixtures 3–5.

> **TL;DR** — On six-icon rows the gilded purple rune in cell 6 is framed in only one row of six. The icon-row locator places every band 4–8 px below the cells (or 8 px too tall), which puts the silver cell's light frame right at the border-detection threshold and lets the lattice drift 16–22 px right of the gold frame. Pin the band's bottom on the cells' dark bevel line and snap its height to the cells' width, stop rewarding rows with exactly one gilded cell, and lock it with a new fixture.

## Problem / Motivation

On a 2560x1440 Combinations panel with six-icon rows (`E:\Git\RuneshapeCaptures\incoming\2026-09-13-purple-gilded-missed.png`, capture region 663x715), every row has a gilded rune in cell 2 and a gilded purple rune in cell 6. The marker overlay frames all seven cell-2 runes but only one of the six purple cell-6 runes (row 4). The dropped cells are classified `Ambiguous` and skipped with a Debug-only log, so at the default Information level nothing shows.

## Root cause (measured on the capture)

The gold frame of cell 6 sits at x=273–275 / 322–324 in **every** row; the game draws all six identically. The difference is in `RuneIconFingerprinter.LocateIconRow`:

- The cells' true extent is 45 px tall with a **dark bevel line** (HSV value < 0.25, ≥78% of the icon strip's columns) at y=45, 153, 261, 369, 477, 585. The located bands were [9,53], [105,157], [224,268], [320,374], [439,483], [537,589]: 4–8 px low, or 53–55 px tall.
- `ScorePlacement` is flat across those shifts (cell count dominates and every shifted band still segments six cells), so `RowDistancePenalty` pulls the band down towards the text line, and the 53 px candidate (text height 28 × `IconToTextHeightRatio` 1.9) beats the 45 px one on tie-breaks.
- **Consequence 1 (rows 0, 2):** with the band 6–8 px low, border columns cover only 37–39 of the 39 rows `BorderColumnCoverage` demands. The silver-framed cell 5 and cell 4's right border drop out; `SegmentIconCells` pairs 169→223 (56 px) and 223→324; `RegulariseToLattice` then takes pitch 58 and width 52 from the decorated left-hand cells and rebuilds cell 6 at x=289.
- **Consequence 2 (rows 1, 3, 5):** a 53 px band makes `CellWidthMinRatio` reject the real 45 px right borders, cells pair one border too far (55–56 px), pitch inflates to 60, cell 6 lands at x=295.
- **Consequence 3 (all rows):** the ring-separation term `bestRing − restRing` rewards a band in which exactly one cell reads gold, so a row with two gilded cells is scored *against* its correct placement (both ≈0.30 → separation ≈0) and *for* the misplaced one (0.22 vs 0.04).

On the correct band [433,477] every border column covers 41–45 of 45 rows, and in row 4 (where cell 5's columns happened to scrape 39/39) segmentation is already right.

## Implementation plan

1. **Score the bevel in `ScorePlacement`** (`src/OCR/RuneIconFingerprinter.cs`). After `SegmentIconCells`, measure the fraction of `IsDarkAt` pixels along `y = bottom` over the x-span from the first cell's left to the last cell's right (span-relative, so two-icon rows on `2 Raw.png` score the same as six-icon rows). Add `fraction × BevelLineWeight` (new constant, ~40 000: above the ring term's ceiling of 6 000 and a 9 px text-distance penalty of 3 600, below one cell's 100 000). Reuses `IsDarkAt` and `DarkLineMaxValue`, which `LocateIconRowByInkRuns` already uses for the same line.
2. **Replace the ring-separation term** with the largest gap between consecutive rings sorted descending (the natural two-cluster split). A row with one or two gilded cells scores its correct band equally; a row with none stays near zero. Keep the 20 000 weight.
3. **Snap the band to square cells in `LocateIconRow`.** After the best placement is chosen, take the median width of its non-gilded cells; if it is within `SquareSnapTolerance` (new constant, 8 px) of the band height, keep `bottom` and set `top = bottom − width + 1`. Cells are square in the game, so the width — measured from dark borders — is the better height. Do not snap when fewer than two plain cells exist (single gilded cell rows on `2 Raw.png`).
4. **Fixture.** Copy the capture to `tests/fixtures/runeicons/2560x1440/6 Raw.png` (same 663x715 region as fixtures 1–5). Add `RuneTwoGildedRowFixtureTests` (`tests/src/OCR/`) modelled on `RuneNarrowRowFixtureTests`: 7 rows, icon counts [6,6,6,6,6,6,4], gilded at index 1 in every row and index 5 in rows 0–5; assert zero ring overlap with the existing 0.20/0.08 margins, `ExtractRowKeys` yields 2 keys in rows 0–5 and 1 in row 6, every cell height within [38,60], and each row's two keys are ≥16 bits apart.
5. **Regression.** `1 Raw.png` and `2 Raw.png` tests (`RuneIconFingerprinterFixtureTests`, `RuneNarrowRowFixtureTests`, `RuneMarkerFixtureTests`, `RuneCropStabilityDiagnostics`) must stay green; identity hashes are plate-anchored (`FindPlateBounds`) so a vertical band shift of ≤8 px must not move them.

Open Questions (non-blocking) — using default: the Debug-only "ambiguous — dropped" log stays at Debug; `ExtractRowKeys` runs per OCR cycle and an Information line there would spam.

## Acceptance criteria

- [ ] On `6 Raw.png`, rows 0–5 each yield exactly two gilded keys (cells 2 and 6) and row 6 yields one; no plain cell is gilded or ambiguous.
- [ ] Gilded rings ≥ 0.20 and plain rings ≤ 0.08 on `6 Raw.png`, with zero overlap.
- [ ] Every located band on `6 Raw.png` ends on the dark bevel line (bottom ∈ {45,153,261,369,477,585,693}) and is 45 px tall in the six-icon rows.
- [ ] All existing rune fixture tests pass unchanged.

## Recommended Tests

Fixture-level (`dotnet test tests/Tests.csproj --filter FullyQualifiedName~Rune`): the new fixture test above plus the four existing fixture classes. The unit test `SegmentIconCells_SyntheticBorderedCells_FindsEachCellAndFlagsTheGoldOne` covers the synthetic path and should be unaffected since it feeds `SegmentIconCells` directly.

1. Markers look squished / mis-sized, "especially the ones that have overflown".

- [ ] No fixture regresses on gilded detection, and ring separation (best minus runner-up) does not shrink on any row.
- [ ] `RuneCropStabilityDiagnostics` drift stays at 0 bits.
- [ ] `NoTwoRowsClaimTheSameIcons` still holds.
- [ ] Decide `RowDistancePenalty`: keep with evidence, or remove.

structuredContent.title: Derive cell height from cell width — cells are square, but height is measured per row

history.comment: Created ticket.

structuredContent.body:
## Symptom

Two things the user has reported repeatedly turn out to be one bug:

1. Markers look squished / mis-sized, "especially the ones that have overflown".
2. Runes in some rows classify as *ambiguous* (gold ring 0.110–0.190) instead of cleanly plain or cleanly gilded, so they get no marker at all.

## Measurement

On `tests/fixtures/runeicons/2560x1440/5 Raw.png` (live capture from the user's panel), `LocateIconRow` returns these row heights:

```
41, 42, 43, 45, 49, 53
```

The cells in that panel are **~52 square**. Width is now measured correctly — the lattice work (RUNE-16 / PR #22) fixed the horizontal geometry. The vertical extent is still found independently per row by scanning for the icon band, and it under-measures by up to 11px on rows where the band blends into the row text or the row is clipped.

Rows 5 and 7 of that capture are the ambiguous ones. A short box crops the gilded frame's top and bottom arcs out of the sample, which is exactly the part of the ring that carries the gold.

## The fix

Rune cells are square. Once the lattice has a confident cell **width**, the height is that width — the row's vertical placement is then a centring problem (where does the square sit), not a measurement problem.

Sketch:
- `RegulariseToLattice` already produces a confident `cellWidth`. Use it as the height.
- Keep `LocateIconRow`'s result only as a *centre* hint: place the square so its centre matches the detected band's centre, clamped inside the row zone.
- `RowDistancePenalty` (currently an unproven guard — the RUNE-12 fixture passes with it at 0) may become redundant once the height stops varying; check whether it can go.

## Why this is its own pass

This moves every cell's box by a few pixels, and the box is what `GoldHueRingProportion` samples. It changes **classification**, not just drawing — rows that currently read correctly could flip. It must be measured against all five fixtures before and after, not bolted onto a UI change.

## Validation

Fixtures: `1 Raw.png` (6 rows), `2 Raw.png` (5 rows, 2-icon rows, one hovered), `3 Raw.png` (10 rows), `4 Raw.png` (8 rows, 8-icon rows), `5 Raw.png` (live capture).

## Acceptance

- [ ] Every row's cell height equals its cell width, within a pixel.
- [ ] `5 Raw.png` rows 5 and 7 read cleanly plain (ring well below the gilded band) rather than 0.110–0.190.
- [ ] No fixture regresses on gilded detection, and ring separation (best minus runner-up) does not shrink on any row.
- [ ] `RuneCropStabilityDiagnostics` drift stays at 0 bits.
- [ ] `NoTwoRowsClaimTheSameIcons` still holds.
- [ ] Decide `RowDistancePenalty`: keep with evidence, or remove.

Re-measured 6 Raw.png: decoy dark line at y=700 reads 0.913 over row 6's cell span vs 0.870 for the true bevel at y=693 — the decoy BEATS the genuine bevel, and RowDistancePenalty (line 417, penalises distance from band centre to the text line below) pushes the same way, so ~4.5k of score favours the wrong band. New Major 4: the uncommitted implementation flips Median (line 930) from upper- to lower-middle, changing RegulariseToLattice pitch/origin/cellWidth on every capture — not in the plan. input.message:
**CHANGES NEEDED** (plan review, pass 2) — the plan body is **unchanged** since the pass-1 review (`bodyVersion c0b1b21513486cb4`), so none of the four requested changes have been made; every prior finding stands. I re-measured the fixture independently and **Major 3 is worse than pass 1 reported**, plus there is a **new Major 4** in the uncommitted implementation.

## Major 3 (re-measured, strengthened) — the decoy outscores the real bevel

I decoded `tests/fixtures/runeicons/2560x1440/6 Raw.png` (663x715) and applied `IsDarkAt`'s exact rule (HSV value < `DarkLineMaxValue` 0.25, i.e. `max(r,g,b) < 64`) per scanline. Dark fraction over row 6's own cell span (x=7..213 — the span `DarkLineFraction` would use, since it runs `cells[0].Bounds.Left`..`cells[^1].Bounds.Right - 1`):

| y | fraction over x=7..213 | longest dark run |
|---|---|---|
| **693** (true bevel) | **0.870** | 45 px [7-51] |
| 694-698 | 0.000 | — |
| 699 | 0.502 | 27 px [206-232] |
| **700** (decoy) | **0.913** | **191 px [0-190]** |
| 701 | 0.541 | 59 px |
| **713** (capture bottom edge) | **0.952** | 171 px [0-170] |

The decoy at y=700 does not merely tie the genuine bevel — it **beats it**, 0.913 vs 0.870, worth `40,000 x 0.043 = ~1,720` in favour of the wrong band.

And `RowDistancePenalty` is not the backstop pass 1 assumed. `src/OCR/RuneIconFingerprinter.cs:417` penalises `|bandCentre - textCentreY|`, and the plan's own root cause states the text line sits **below** the icons ("`RowDistancePenalty` pulls the band down towards the text line"). Shifting the band 7 px down to y=700 therefore moves it **towards** the text and **earns back** `7 x 400 = 2,800`. Both terms point at the decoy: **~4,500 of score favours the wrong placement**, and the plan's own root-cause section says cell count is flat across shifts this small ("every shifted band still segments six cells"). There is nothing left to catch it.

Required: a discriminator that is not raw darkness across a span. Concrete options — require the dark run to be bounded by the segmented cells' *own* border columns (the y=700 run starts at x=0, outside cell 1's left border at x=7, and the true bevel's does not); or require a plausible band *top* as well as bottom; or clamp the candidate's bottom to lie inside the segmented cells. State which, and add row 6's bottom = 693 as a pinned assertion in the new test.

## Major 4 (new) — the implementation changes `Median` globally, and the plan does not mention it

The uncommitted diff on this worktree changes `Median` (`src/OCR/RuneIconFingerprinter.cs:930`) from upper-middle to **lower-middle** (`sorted[(sorted.Length - 1) / 2]`). That function has **8 call sites**, including `RegulariseToLattice`'s `pitch` (line 707), `origin` (line 713) and `cellWidth` (line 718), and the cell-extent normalisation at lines 563/564/573/574. For any even-length input the result changes, so this moves **lattice geometry on every capture** — a larger blast radius than anything the plan describes, and `GoldHueRingProportion` samples the box it produces.

This is precisely the class of change RUNE-19 says "must be measured against all five fixtures before and after". Either add it to the plan with its own justification and before/after evidence, or revert it and keep the lower-middle rule local to `SnapToSquareCells`.

## Major 1 (re-confirmed) — step 3 duplicates open ticket RUNE-19

`RUNE-19` is live on the board (**Todo, High, effort M**, "Derive cell height from cell width — cells are square, but height is measured per row") and specifies the same fix incompatibly: height = width **unconditionally**, with `LocateIconRow`'s band kept only as a **centre** hint, and an explicit ask to decide whether `RowDistancePenalty` can be deleted. RUNE-22 step 3 keeps the band's **bottom** as the anchor and gates the snap on a tolerance. Whichever lands first forces the other to be rewritten.

**Decide in the plan text**: drop step 3 and leave it to RUNE-19 (my recommendation — steps 1 and 2 alone fix the reported bug), or state that RUNE-22 supersedes RUNE-19 and close RUNE-19 as absorbed.

## Major 2 (re-confirmed against the code) — `SquareSnapTolerance = 8` misses its own targets

The implemented guard is `if (cellWidth < MinCellPx || Math.Abs(cellWidth - rowHeight) > SquareSnapTolerance) return (top, bottom);` — so delta 8 snaps, delta 9+ does not. Against that:

- This ticket's "Consequence 2" measures bands **53-55 px** against a true width of **45** — deltas **8-10**. The 55 px case, one of the rows the ticket is filed about, **does not snap**.
- RUNE-19 records `LocateIconRow` heights of **41, 42, 43, 45, 49, 53** on `5 Raw.png` against ~52 px square cells — deltas up to **11**. None of the worst rows snap.

A tolerance that declines to act precisely where width and height disagree most defeats its own stated purpose. Re-derive it against the 10-11 px deltas on record, or adopt RUNE-19's unconditional form.

## Minor 1 — the plate-anchoring regression claim is wrong on one path

Step 5 says "identity hashes are plate-anchored (`FindPlateBounds`) so a vertical band shift of <=8 px must not move them". `ExtractRowKeys` falls back to `Inset(cell.GlyphBounds, GlyphInsetRatio)` when `FindPlateBounds` returns null; on that path the hash **does** follow the band. Soften the claim, or point at `RuneCropStabilityDiagnostics` as the thing that actually enforces it.

## Minor 2 — fixtures 3, 4, 5 have no asserting test

`RuneRowGeometryDiagnostics` is the only class touching `3/4/5 Raw.png` and every method is a `Dump*` with zero `Assert` calls, so it cannot fail. Given Major 4 moves geometry on every capture, have the implementer run `DumpRowGeometry` before and after and paste the diff into this ticket.

## Verified correct — do not re-litigate

- Every cited symbol and constant exists and means what the plan says: `LocateIconRow`, `ScorePlacement`, `RowDistancePenalty = 400` (line 171), `CellWidthMinRatio = 0.85`, `BorderColumnCoverage = 0.85`, `IsDarkAt` (line 942), `DarkLineMaxValue = 0.25` (line 126), `RegulariseToLattice`.
- The **span-relative** bevel measurement in step 1 is correct and load-bearing: row 6 reads **0.870** over its own span but only **0.571** over the six-icon span (x=7..321), so an absolute-width measure would fail exactly that row. Acceptance criterion 3's `y=693` is confirmed by measurement.
- `DetectCells` re-runs `SegmentIconCells` on the band `LocateIconRow` returns, so snapping `top` is safely re-segmented afterwards.
- **Step 4 needs no build change**: `6 Raw.png` is already on disk at 663x715 and `tests/Tests.csproj:34` copies it via the `fixtures\runeicons\**\*.png` glob.
- Artifact flag (W1) not applicable — detection geometry, no new UI component, layout or interaction.

## To clear this gate

1. Resolve the RUNE-19 overlap in the plan text (drop step 3, or supersede RUNE-19 explicitly).
2. If step 3 stays, re-derive `SquareSnapTolerance` against the 10-11 px deltas and keep the `>` comparison documented.
3. Add a real discriminator for the y=700 / y=713 decoys — darkness-over-span alone loses to y=700 by ~4,500 once `RowDistancePenalty` is counted.
4. Bring the global `Median` change into the plan with justification and fixture evidence, or revert it.
5. Fix the plate-anchoring claim; add the before/after `DumpRowGeometry` run for fixtures 3-5.

1. **Decoy dark line beats the real bevel.** I re-decoded `6 Raw.png` with `IsDarkAt`'s exact rule: over row 6's own cell span (x=7..213) the true bevel at y=693 reads **0.870** but the decoy line at y=700 reads **0.913** (and the capture's bottom edge at y=713 reads 0.952). The new 40,000-weight term therefore *prefers* the wrong band by ~1,720 — and `RowDistancePenalty` (line 417) penalises distance from the band centre to the text line *below*, so shifting down 7 px earns back another 2,800. ~4,500 of score points at the wrong placement and the plan's own root cause says cell count is flat across shifts that small. Needs a real discriminator (e.g. require the dark run to be bounded by the cells' own border columns — the y=700 run starts at x=0, outside cell 1's left border at x=7).

2. **The uncommitted implementation changes `Median` globally** (line 930, upper- to lower-middle) across 8 call sites including `RegulariseToLattice`'s pitch/origin/cellWidth. That moves lattice geometry on every capture and is nowhere in the plan. Justify it with before/after fixture evidence, or revert it and keep the rule local to `SnapToSquareCells`.

3. **Step 3 duplicates open ticket RUNE-19**, which specifies the same square-snap incompatibly (height = width unconditionally, band as a *centre* hint). Drop step 3, or supersede RUNE-19 explicitly.

4. **`SquareSnapTolerance = 8` misses its own targets.** The implemented guard is `> SquareSnapTolerance`, so the ticket's own 10 px case and RUNE-19's 11 px rows never snap.

Minors: the "hashes are plate-anchored" claim ignores the `Inset(GlyphBounds)` fallback; fixtures 3-5 have no asserting test (`RuneRowGeometryDiagnostics` is Dump-only).

Verified good: all cited symbols and constants match; the span-relative bevel design is correct and load-bearing (row 6 reads 0.870 over its own span vs 0.571 over the six-icon span); `DetectCells` re-segments after `LocateIconRow`; step 4 needs no build change — `6 Raw.png` is on disk at 663x715 and the `Tests.csproj` glob already copies it.

## Problem / Motivation

On a 2560x1440 Combinations panel with six-icon rows (`E:\Git\RuneshapeCaptures\incoming\2026-09-13-purple-gilded-missed.png`, capture region 663x715), every row has a gilded rune in cell 2 and a gilded purple rune in cell 6. The dropped cells are classified `Ambiguous` and skipped with a Debug-only log, so at the default Information level nothing shows.

## Root cause (measured on the capture)

The gold frame of cell 6 sits at x=273–275 / 322–324 in **every** row; the game draws all six identically. The difference is in `RuneIconFingerprinter.LocateIconRow`:

- The cells' true extent is 45 px tall with a **dark bevel line** (HSV value < 0.25, ≥78% of the icon strip's columns) at y=45, 153, 261, 369, 477, 585. The located bands were [9,53], [105,157], [224,268], [320,374], [439,483], [537,589]: 4–8 px low, or 53–55 px tall.

- **Consequence 1 (rows 0, 2):** with the band 6–8 px low, border columns cover only 37–39 of the 39 rows `BorderColumnCoverage` demands. The silver-framed cell 5 and cell 4's right border drop out; `SegmentIconCells` pairs 169→223 (56 px) and 223→324; `RegulariseToLattice` then takes pitch 58 and width 52 from the decorated left-hand cells and rebuilds cell 6 at x=289.
- **Consequence 2 (rows 1, 3, 5):** a 53 px band makes `CellWidthMinRatio` reject the real 45 px right borders, cells pair one border too far (55–56 px), pitch inflates to 60, cell 6 lands at x=295.
- **Consequence 3 (all rows):** the ring-separation term `bestRing − restRing` rewards a band in which exactly one cell reads gold, so a row with two gilded cells is scored *against* its correct placement (both ≈0.30 → separation ≈0) and *for* the misplaced one (0.22 vs 0.04).

2. **Replace the ring-separation term** with the largest gap between consecutive rings sorted descending (the natural two-cluster split). A row with one or two gilded cells scores its correct band equally; a row with none stays near zero. Keep the 20 000 weight.
3. **Snap the band to square cells in `LocateIconRow`.** After the best placement is chosen, take the median width of its non-gilded cells; if it is within `SquareSnapTolerance` (new constant, 8 px) of the band height, keep `bottom` and set `top = bottom − width + 1`. The icon-row locator places every band 4–8 px below the cells (or 8 px too tall), which puts the silver cell's light frame right at the border-detection threshold and lets the lattice drift 16–22 px right of the gold frame. Pin the band's bottom on the cells' dark bevel line and snap its height to the cells' width, stop rewarding rows with exactly one gilded cell, and lock it with a new fixture.

## Problem / Motivation

On a 2560x1440 Combinations panel with six-icon rows (`E:\Git\RuneshapeCaptures\incoming\2026-09-13-purple-gilded-missed.png`, capture region 663x715), every row has a gilded rune in cell 2 and a gilded purple rune in cell 6. The marker overlay frames all seven cell-2 runes but only one of the six purple cell-6 runes (row 4). The dropped cells are classified `Ambiguous` and skipped with a Debug-only log, so at the default Information level nothing shows.

## Root cause (measured on the capture)

The gold frame of cell 6 sits at x=273–275 / 322–324 in **every** row; the game draws all six identically. The difference is in `RuneIconFingerprinter.LocateIconRow`:

- The cells' true extent is 45 px tall with a **dark bevel line** (HSV value < 0.25, ≥78% of the icon strip's columns) at y=45, 153, 261, 369, 477, 585. The located bands were [9,53], [105,157], [224,268], [320,374], [439,483], [537,589]: 4–8 px low, or 53–55 px tall.
- `ScorePlacement` is flat across those shifts (cell count dominates and every shifted band still segments six cells), so `RowDistancePenalty` pulls the band down towards the text line, and the 53 px candidate (text height 28 × `IconToTextHeightRatio` 1.9) beats the 45 px one on tie-breaks.
- **Consequence 1 (rows 0, 2):** with the band 6–8 px low, border columns cover only 37–39 of the 39 rows `BorderColumnCoverage` demands. The silver-framed cell 5 and cell 4's right border drop out; `SegmentIconCells` pairs 169→223 (56 px) and 223→324; `RegulariseToLattice` then takes pitch 58 and width 52 from the decorated left-hand cells and rebuilds cell 6 at x=289.
- **Consequence 2 (rows 1, 3, 5):** a 53 px band makes `CellWidthMinRatio` reject the real 45 px right borders, cells pair one border too far (55–56 px), pitch inflates to 60, cell 6 lands at x=295.
- **Consequence 3 (all rows):** the ring-separation term `bestRing − restRing` rewards a band in which exactly one cell reads gold, so a row with two gilded cells is scored *against* its correct placement (both ≈0.30 → separation ≈0) and *for* the misplaced one (0.22 vs 0.04).

On the correct band [433,477] every border column covers 41–45 of 45 rows, and in row 4 (where cell 5's columns happened to scrape 39/39) segmentation is already right.

## Implementation plan

1. **Score the bevel in `ScorePlacement`** (`src/OCR/RuneIconFingerprinter.cs`). After `SegmentIconCells`, measure the fraction of `IsDarkAt` pixels along `y = bottom` over the x-span from the first cell's left to the last cell's right (span-relative, so two-icon rows on `2 Raw.png` score the same as six-icon rows). Add `fraction × BevelLineWeight` (new constant, ~40 000: above the ring term's ceiling of 6 000 and a 9 px text-distance penalty of 3 600, below one cell's 100 000). Reuses `IsDarkAt` and `DarkLineMaxValue`, which `LocateIconRowByInkRuns` already uses for the same line.
2. **Replace the ring-separation term** with the largest gap between consecutive rings sorted descending (the natural two-cluster split). A row with one or two gilded cells scores its correct band equally; a row with none stays near zero. Keep the 20 000 weight.
3. **Snap the band to square cells in `LocateIconRow`.** After the best placement is chosen, take the median width of its non-gilded cells; if it is within `SquareSnapTolerance` (new constant, 8 px) of the band height, keep `bottom` and set `top = bottom − width + 1`. Cells are square in the game, so the width — measured from dark borders — is the better height. Do not snap when fewer than two plain cells exist (single gilded cell rows on `2 Raw.png`).
4. **Fixture.** Copy the capture to `tests/fixtures/runeicons/2560x1440/6 Raw.png` (same 663x715 region as fixtures 1–5). Add `RuneTwoGildedRowFixtureTests` (`tests/src/OCR/`) modelled on `RuneNarrowRowFixtureTests`: 7 rows, icon counts [6,6,6,6,6,6,4], gilded at index 1 in every row and index 5 in rows 0–5; assert zero ring overlap with the existing 0.20/0.08 margins, `ExtractRowKeys` yields 2 keys in rows 0–5 and 1 in row 6, every cell height within [38,60], and each row's two keys are ≥16 bits apart.
5. **Regression.** `1 Raw.png` and `2 Raw.png` tests (`RuneIconFingerprinterFixtureTests`, `RuneNarrowRowFixtureTests`, `RuneMarkerFixtureTests`, `RuneCropStabilityDiagnostics`) must stay green; identity hashes are plate-anchored (`FindPlateBounds`) so a vertical band shift of ≤8 px must not move them.

Open Questions (non-blocking) — using default: the Debug-only "ambiguous — dropped" log stays at Debug; `ExtractRowKeys` runs per OCR cycle and an Information line there would spam.

## Acceptance criteria

- [ ] On `6 Raw.png`, rows 0–5 each yield exactly two gilded keys (cells 2 and 6) and row 6 yields one; no plain cell is gilded or ambiguous.
- [ ] Gilded rings ≥ 0.20 and plain rings ≤ 0.08 on `6 Raw.png`, with zero overlap.
- [ ] Every located band on `6 Raw.png` ends on the dark bevel line (bottom ∈ {45,153,261,369,477,585,693}) and is 45 px tall in the six-icon rows.
- [ ] All existing rune fixture tests pass unchanged.

## Recommended Tests

Fixture-level (`dotnet test tests/Tests.csproj --filter FullyQualifiedName~Rune`): the new fixture test above plus the four existing fixture classes.
